text: Picking individual stocks? It can be confusing, and seriously time consuming. But ETFs make investing easy. An ETF is a bundle of stocks you can buy as one. Think of it like grabbing a carton of eggs, instead of picking twelve, one at a time. ETFs group stocks by industry, by location, or by company size. Some ETFs even track the entire stock market, like SPY and VOO, which both follow the S and P 500. One purchase. Hundreds of stocks. Instant diversification. And many ETFs also pay dividends, quarterly payouts, just for holding the shares. Next, we'll break down how ETFs work, and what to watch out for.
